properties.name: 31 request fields publish their enum, and a guard now fails the build when a declared enum is neither wired nor exempt
properties.rationale:
CLOSES THE CLASS F-19's `contained_symptom` STOOD IN FOR. That repair fixed `Requirement.concern` and recorded that the proper fix was "a check that every declared enum reachable through a request field publishes its values, so the next one cannot ship unwired". This is that check.

⚠️ THE COUNT WAS PUT TO THE USER WRONG THREE TIMES, and that is the argument for the guard rather than a footnote to it. A name-matching sweep of service.rs said ~40 — it matched any same-NAMED field on any struct, so two different `concern` fields counted off one hit. A per-struct sweep with an incomplete type map said ~3. The checked answer is 31. Each attempt was wrong in a different direction, and the difference between them was a judgement a human had to make each time; a standing check is what stops that judgement being re-made from scratch.

🛑 A NAME SWEEP WOULD HAVE WIRED FIVE FIELDS WRONGLY, which is why the wired list is hand-made and the test does not derive it. The sharpest is `add_component`'s `level`: the decomposition ladder is DELIBERATELY OPEN and per-project (`Project.decomposition_levels`), settled in `dec:the-decomposition-ladder-is-open-not-a-fixed-enum`. Publishing a fixed set there would assert every domain bottoms out at the same depth AND contradict an accepted decision. The others: `DesignRule.category` is free text by design, the two readiness `level` fields are a 1-9 TRL rung refused outside range, and two more are query parameters rather than node properties at all.

⭐ THE EXEMPT LIST IS ALSO A FINDING. 33 declared enums are exempt and only five are exempt for meaning something else; THE OTHER 28 ARE EXEMPT BECAUSE NO TYPED CALL CAN WRITE THEM — 17 edge properties reachable only through create_edge's free-JSON `props` map, and 11 node properties reachable only through create_node's. Declared, validated, and unreachable from the path every skill points at: the class `fact:a-third-of-declared-properties-name-nothing-any-tool-accepts` records. Publishing their values would not help because nothing can pass them; giving them parameters is a larger question. The list is where that backlog is now visible rather than implied.

THE GUARD'S OWN FIRST RUN WAS WRONG AND THE FIX IS RECORDED IN IT: it parsed `schema_enum!` line by line, and `cargo fmt` wraps long invocations across four lines, so it reported 41 unwired of which a dozen were wired. A guard wrong in the SAFE direction is still wrong — it would have had somebody write exemptions for fields that did not need them. It now reads the whole file. Its staleness half then caught a second error: four of the five "must not wire" entries were not declared enums at all, only name-collisions with another type's, so they never belonged in a list keyed on declared enums.

REPAIR: `corrected_cause` for the class, recorded here because `repair` cannot ride this call — see `fact:record-change-places-an-event-by-epoch-and-212-of-214-epochs-carry-no-date`.
properties.subject: system
properties.summary: 31 request fields across 26 tools now publish their type's declared enum values, wired through `schema_enum!` so the list is read from the compiled-in schema. The surface went from 47 to 78 top-level properties publishing an enum. A new test, `every_declared_enum_is_wired_or_exempt`, asserts both halves: every wired field publishes the schema's OWN values, and every declared enum is either wired or named EXEMPT with a reason — so a newly declared enum fails the build until somebody decides which it is.
